summary: Defines an UNSELECT command for IMAP4 that closes the current mailbox without expunging it. Some clients need to release resources tied to the selected mailbox without selecting another one, which IMAP4 previously did only through awkward workarounds. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: UNSELECT closes the currently selected IMAP mailbox but leaves messages marked for deletion in place. It returns the session to the authenticated state.

questions: how to close an imap mailbox without expunge
how do i close an imap mailbox without expunging
how does an imap server advertise unselect
subtitle: An IMAP command that closes the selected mailbox without expunging deleted messages.

tldr.problem: IMAP clients need to release resources for a selected mailbox without deleting messages marked for deletion.
tldr.mechanism: UNSELECT closes the selected mailbox and returns the server to the authenticated state, like CLOSE but without expunging messages.
tldr.outcome: Servers advertise the UNSELECT capability, and clients have a direct command for leaving a mailbox without expunging it.

today: RFC 3691 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Closing a Mailbox Without Expunging
sections.content:
Some IMAP clients need to release resources for a selected mailbox without selecting another one. The existing CLOSE command closes the mailbox and permanently removes messages marked with the \Deleted flag.

IMAP lacked a command that simply closed the selected mailbox without expunging it. This RFC adds UNSELECT for that purpose.
sections.plainLanguage: A client may need to stop using a mailbox without deleting its marked messages. UNSELECT provides that action.

sections.title: The UNSELECT Command
sections.content:
UNSELECT takes no arguments. It frees server resources associated with the selected mailbox and returns the server to the authenticated state. It performs the same actions as CLOSE except that no messages are permanently removed.

The command returns OK when it completes. It returns BAD if no mailbox is selected or if an argument is supplied. Its syntax is case-insensitive.
sections.plainLanguage: The client sends UNSELECT with no arguments. The server closes the mailbox but does not permanently remove messages marked for deletion.

sections.title: Capability and Registration
sections.content:
A server that supports the command advertises the capability name UNSELECT. The RFC adds UNSELECT as a command-select form and registers the capability with IANA.

The security section says the extension adds no security concerns beyond those already discussed in the IMAP specification.
sections.plainLanguage: A supporting server announces UNSELECT so clients can know the command is available. The RFC says the extension adds no new security concerns.
